**Chapter 11: Mineral Resources: Fossils**

**Section 11.03: Different Polymers, Properties and Uses**

**Table 11.03: Different Polymers, Properties and Uses**

| **Name of the polymer** | **Formula of monomer** | **Properties of polymer** | **Uses** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Polyethylene | CH2=CH2 | Cannot be easily, durable | Plastic bag, plastic sheet |
| Polypropene | CH2=CH-CH3 | Cannot be easily, durable | Plastic rope, plastic bottle |
| Polyvinyl chloride(PVC) | CH2=CHCl | Hard, solid and less flexible than polyethylene | Water pipe, electric insulator |
| Nylon 6:6 | HOOC-(CH2)4-COOH & H2N-(CH2)6-NH2 | Glittering, durable, flexible | Artificial cloths, rope, tooth brush |

**Synthetic polymer or plastic**

Plastic is hard, light, cheap and available in any colour. Plastic can be melted and be given any shape by molding. The word plastic has come from the Greek word 'Plastikos' which means possible to melt. Many of us make various materials by melting rejected plastic parts. It is dangerous because burning or melting of plastic products by heating produces many toxic gases. Plastic is widely used to produce various products like pots for keeping foods, packets, ballpens, chairs, tables, motor parts, water tanks, bowls, buckets, mugs etc.
